    Ovsienko's theorem (radical vector with a coordinate one, coordinates at most six) #

    A critical unit form in at least three variables is nonnegative of corank one, and its radical is generated by a positive vector z with some coordinate z_c = 1 (Critical.ovsienko; Ovsienko, see von Höhne 1988, §1). The proof inflates to a graph form (UnitForms/Reduction.lean), treats graph forms by their patterns (UnitForms/Graph.lean, UnitForms/Tree.lean) and pulls the vector back.

    Corank one with a positive radical vector (at least three points) gives Good.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Forms.UnitForm.Critical.ovsienko {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (q : UnitForm ι) (hq : q.Critical) (hn : 3 ≤ Fintype.card ι) :
    (∀ (x : ι → ℤ), 0 ≤ q.val x) ∧ ∃ (z : ι → ℤ) (c : ι), (∀ (a : ι), 0 < z a) ∧ (∀ (x : ι → ℤ), q.B z x = 0) ∧ z c = 1 ∧ (∀ (a : ι), z a ≤ 6) ∧ ∀ (x : ι → ℤ), q.val x = 0 → x = x c • z

    Ovsienko's theorem. A critical unit form in at least three variables is nonnegative, and there are a positive radical vector z with all coordinates at most 6 and a point c with z_c = 1 such that every x with q(x) = 0 is x_c • z.
